message.content:
For the congruence
\[
8x \equiv 1 \pmod p
\]
to have a solution modulo a prime \(p\), we need \(\gcd(8,p)\) to divide \(1\).

- If \(p\neq 2\), then \(p\) is odd, so \(\gcd(8,p)=1\), which divides \(1\). Thus a solution exists.
- If \(p=2\), then \(8\equiv 0\pmod 2\), so the congruence becomes
  \[
  0x\equiv 1\pmod 2,
  \]
  i.e.
  \[
  0\equiv 1\pmod 2,
  \]
  which is impossible.

Thus the only prime for which there is no solution is \(p=2\). The sum of all such primes is
\[
2.
\]

The answer is 2.
